subject: Civic Education
competence: Controls the emotions in such a way that it safeguards the existence of a democratic society.
lesson: Accepts the view that the positively control of emotions as a democratic citizen bring about the betterment of the person as well as the society: Institutional Fact-Finding Station: Competency Level 8.2.3
unique_learning_outcome: Accepts the view that the positively control of emotions as a democratic citizen bring about the betterment of the person as well as the society.
Describes giving examples the nature of various kinds of emotions occuring in a person.
the_entrance: 5-minute introduction: The teacher writes or reads “Accepts the view that the positively control of emotions as a democratic citizen bring about the betterment of the person as well as the society” and asks students to name one example they have seen in everyday life. Students share brief responses; the teacher connects their examples to Institutional Fact-Finding Station: Competency Level 8.2.3 and explains how it will help them explore this period's outcome.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher introduces the lesson inquiry on 'Accepts the view that the positively control of emotions as a democratic citizen bring about the betterment of the person as well as the society', organizes students into collaborative teams with designated roles, and distributes inquiry task prompt cards.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Students arrange themselves in assigned group roles, examine the inquiry prompt concerning 'Accepts the view that the positively control of emotions as a democratic citizen bring about the betterment of the person as well as the society', and prepare materials for their investigation.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Inquiry prompt cards, chalkboard, student notebooks

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher actively circulates among the groups to facilitate Institutional Fact-Finding Station: Competency Level 8.2.3, scaffolds student discussions around 'Accepts the view that the positively control of emotions as a democratic citizen bring about the betterment of the person as well as the society', prompts critical thinking, and formatively monitors student engagement.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Students actively carry out Institutional Fact-Finding Station: Competency Level 8.2.3, collaborating in teams to analyze real-world civic situations related to 'Accepts the view that the positively control of emotions as a democratic citizen bring about the betterment of the person as well as the society' without passive bystanders.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Activity scenario cards, observation sheets, chart paper

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher facilitates group presentations, synthesizes student discoveries regarding 'Accepts the view that the positively control of emotions as a democratic citizen bring about the betterment of the person as well as the society', highlights core civic values, and formatively clarifies any conceptual misconceptions.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Team spokespersons present their group's findings on 'Accepts the view that the positively control of emotions as a democratic citizen bring about the betterment of the person as well as the society' to the class, compare conclusions with peers, and record constructive feedback in their notebooks.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Presentation board, student summary sheets, whiteboard

summary: Synthesize key student findings from Institutional Fact-Finding Station: Competency Level 8.2.3, emphasizing the core principles of “Accepts the view that the positively control of emotions as a democratic citizen bring about the betterment of the person as well as the society” and clarifying any lingering misconceptions.
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: Use the student's five-minute assignment response to check understanding of “Accepts the view that the positively control of emotions as a democratic citizen bring about the betterment of the person as well as the society” and give one concise correction or affirmation.
post_activity: 5-minute in-class assignment: Each student completes a short exit response explaining one finding about “Accepts the view that the positively control of emotions as a democratic citizen bring about the betterment of the person as well as the society” using evidence or an example from Institutional Fact-Finding Station: Competency Level 8.2.3. The teacher reviews responses for an accurate link to the period outcome.
